display_name: Retail Credit Scoring — Champion vs Challenger Revalidation

governed_model.use_case: Retail lending PD estimation and adverse-action reasons

workflow.name: retail-credit-scoring-model
workflow.description: 4-step retail credit decision: applicant assessment, PD estimation, adverse-action reasons, and final decision — for the model that assists retail lending officers.

eval_run.name: Annual Revalidation — Champion v3 vs Challenger v4
eval_run.description: Independent revalidation of the retail credit decisioning model against the in-production champion. Tests output stability, PD alignment, and the regulatory adequacy of adverse-action reasons. Supports CBUAE MMS ongoing monitoring and SR 11-7 outcomes analysis.

cases.label: personal-loan-strong-salaried
cases.application: Personal loan AED 120,000, 48 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 28,000/mo, 6 years employment (government-related entity). Existing DBR 22%. AECB score 780. No delinquencies.
cases.aa_a: Stable prime salaried applicant, strong tenure at a GRE employer, low existing leverage. Post-loan DBR ~38%, within the 50% cap.
cases.aa_b: Prime salaried applicant with strong employment tenure and low existing obligations. Post-loan DBR ~38%, comfortably under the regulatory cap.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 0.6% (low). Drivers: high score band, low DBR, long tenure.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 0.7% (low). Drivers: high AECB band, low DBR, stable employment.
cases.dec_a: APPROVE at requested amount and tenor; standard pricing.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE at requested amount and tenor; standard pricing.

cases.label: auto-loan-dbr-breach
cases.application: Auto loan AED 95,000, 60 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 11,000/mo, 2 years employment. Existing obligations: personal loan + 2 credit cards; existing DBR 41%. AECB score 690.
cases.aa_a: Near-prime applicant already carrying high leverage. Adding this loan pushes DBR to ~53%, above the 50% regulatory cap.
cases.aa_b: Near-prime applicant with elevated existing leverage; the new facility takes DBR beyond the 50% cap to ~53%.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 4.8% (elevated), driven primarily by post-loan DBR above cap and mid credit band.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 5.1% (elevated), driven by DBR breach and moderate score.
cases.ar_a: (1) Post-loan debt-burden ratio of ~53% exceeds the 50% maximum; (2) existing unsecured obligations are high relative to income. Reducing tenor does not cure the DBR breach.
cases.ar_b: (1) Debt-burden ratio exceeds policy; (2) credit profile below threshold.
cases.dec_a: DECLINE as structured. Offer a lower amount (~AED 60,000) or longer tenor that brings DBR under 50%.

cases.label: credit-card-thin-file
cases.application: Credit card, AED 30,000 limit. Applicant: salaried, AED 9,500/mo, 8 months employment, first credit facility (thin file). AECB score unavailable (insufficient history). DBR 0%.
cases.aa_a: Thin-file applicant with no bureau history and short tenure; income adequate but track record unproven.
cases.aa_b: Thin-file applicant, no bureau score, short employment tenure; limited basis to assess repayment behaviour.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 6.5% (elevated) with wide uncertainty due to absent bureau data; assign to manual review.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 6.9% (elevated); high uncertainty from thin file — recommend manual review.
cases.ar_a: (1) Insufficient credit history to score; (2) employment tenure below 12 months. Not a decline on capacity — refer to manual underwriting with a reduced starting limit.
cases.ar_b: (1) No credit history available; (2) short employment tenure. Recommend manual review rather than automated decline.
cases.dec_a: REFER to manual underwriting; if approved, start at AED 10,000 limit and review after 6 months of conduct.
cases.dec_b: REFER to manual underwriting; suggested starter limit AED 10,000 with a 6-month conduct review.

cases.label: mortgage-topup-prime
cases.application: Mortgage top-up AED 300,000 on an existing owner-occupied property (current LTV 55%, post-top-up LTV 68%). Applicant: salaried, AED 45,000/mo, 10 years employment. Existing DBR 30%. AECB 805.
cases.aa_a: Prime applicant, strong income and tenure, secured request with post-top-up LTV 68% (within the 80% cap for a first property) and DBR ~40% post-facility.
cases.aa_b: Prime, secured request; post-top-up LTV 68% and DBR ~40%, both within policy.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 0.4% (very low); secured, prime band, ample capacity.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 0.5% (very low); secured and prime.
cases.ar_a: None — within LTV and DBR limits.
cases.ar_b: None — within LTV and DBR limits.
cases.dec_a: APPROVE the top-up; standard secured pricing.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE the top-up; standard secured pricing.

cases.label: personal-loan-recent-delinquency
cases.application: Personal loan AED 70,000, 36 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 16,000/mo, 4 years employment. Existing DBR 28%. AECB 655. One credit-card payment 60+ days past due 5 months ago, since regularised.
cases.aa_a: Mid-band applicant with adequate capacity but a recent 60-DPD event now cured; behaviour risk elevated over the last 6 months.
cases.aa_b: Mid-band applicant, adequate capacity, recent delinquency cured; short seasoning since the event.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 5.9% (elevated); the recent-but-cured 60-DPD event is the dominant driver, partly offset by capacity.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 3.2% (moderate); treats the delinquency as fully resolved and weights current capacity.
cases.ar_a: (1) A recent 60-day delinquency within the last 6 months; (2) credit score in the sub-prime band. Recommend approval at a reduced amount with risk-based pricing once 6 months' clean conduct is evidenced.
cases.ar_b: (1) Credit score below preferred threshold. Delinquency treated as resolved.
cases.dec_a: REFER / conditional approve at AED 40,000 with risk-based pricing; revisit full amount after 6 months clean.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE at requested amount with standard pricing.

cases.label: auto-loan-self-employed
cases.application: Auto loan AED 130,000, 60 months. Applicant: self-employed (trading license 5 years), declared income AED 22,000/mo, bank-statement-verified average credits AED 18,500/mo. Existing DBR 20%. AECB 720.
cases.aa_a: Self-employed applicant; use the bank-statement-verified AED 18,500/mo (not declared AED 22,000) for capacity. Post-loan DBR on verified income ~33%.
cases.aa_b: Self-employed applicant; use verified average credits of AED 18,500/mo. Post-loan DBR ~33% on the verified figure.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 2.6% (moderate); income variability of self-employment is the main uncertainty, capacity otherwise sound.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 2.8% (moderate); self-employment income variability drives the estimate.
cases.ar_a: None on capacity — approve on verified income. Note: assess against verified AED 18,500/mo, not declared income.
cases.dec_a: APPROVE at requested amount using verified income; secured by the vehicle.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE at requested amount using verified income; secured by the vehicle.

cases.label: credit-card-limit-increase
cases.application: Credit-card limit increase from AED 25,000 to AED 60,000. Applicant: salaried, AED 20,000/mo, utilisation last 12 months averaging 85% of current limit, 3 late payments in 12 months. AECB 675. Existing DBR 35%.
cases.aa_a: High-utilisation, occasionally-late cardholder requesting a large limit jump; 85% utilisation with 3 late payments signals repayment stress, not simply demand.
cases.aa_b: Cardholder with high utilisation and some late payments requesting a limit increase; conduct suggests stress.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 7.2% (high); sustained 85% utilisation plus 3 late payments are strong early-delinquency signals.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 7.5% (high); high utilisation and late payments dominate.
cases.ar_a: (1) Sustained high utilisation (~85%) of the existing limit; (2) three late payments in the last 12 months. A limit increase would raise, not relieve, risk. Decline the increase; consider a repayment plan.
cases.ar_b: (1) High utilisation; (2) recent late payments. Decline the increase.
cases.dec_a: DECLINE the increase; offer counselling / structured repayment on the existing limit.

cases.label: personal-loan-high-income-highdbr
cases.application: Personal loan AED 250,000, 48 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 60,000/mo, 12 years employment. Existing DBR 44% (mortgage + car). AECB 760.
cases.aa_a: Prime, high-income applicant but already at 44% DBR; the new loan pushes DBR to ~52%, marginally above the 50% cap despite strong income.
cases.aa_b: Prime high-income applicant near the DBR ceiling; new facility takes DBR to ~52%, just over the cap.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 2.1% (moderate); low intrinsic risk but the DBR breach is a hard policy constraint regardless of score.
cases.ar_a: (1) Post-loan debt-burden ratio ~52% exceeds the 50% cap. High income does not waive the cap. Approve a reduced amount (~AED 180,000) that keeps DBR ≤ 50%.
cases.dec_a: DECLINE as structured; counter-offer ~AED 180,000 to stay within the DBR cap.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE at requested amount; strong income supports the facility.

cases.label: auto-loan-clean-nearprime
cases.application: Auto loan AED 80,000, 60 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 13,500/mo, 3 years employment. Existing DBR 18%. AECB 700. No adverse history.
cases.aa_a: Near-prime applicant with low leverage and clean history; post-loan DBR ~34%, well within cap; secured.
cases.aa_b: Near-prime, low leverage, clean history; post-loan DBR ~34%; secured facility.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 2.0% (moderate-low); clean conduct and low DBR offset the mid score band.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 2.2% (moderate-low); clean conduct, low DBR.
cases.dec_a: APPROVE at requested amount; standard secured pricing.
cases.dec_b: APPROVE at requested amount; standard secured pricing.

cases.label: personal-loan-probation
cases.application: Personal loan AED 50,000, 36 months. Applicant: salaried, AED 14,000/mo, 4 months employment (still on probation), no prior facilities. AECB score limited. DBR 0%.
cases.aa_a: Applicant still within probation period with minimal credit history; income adequate but employment not yet confirmed permanent.
cases.aa_b: Applicant on probation with thin file; employment stability unconfirmed.
cases.pd_a: Estimated 12-month PD 5.4% (elevated); employment-confirmation risk during probation is the main driver.
cases.pd_b: Estimated 12-month PD 5.6% (elevated); probation-period employment risk dominates.
cases.ar_a: (1) Employment still within probation (tenure < 6 months); (2) limited credit history. Recommend deferring until probation is confirmed, then reassess.
cases.ar_b: (1) Employment tenure below policy minimum; (2) limited history. Defer pending confirmation of employment.
cases.dec_a: DEFER; invite reapplication on confirmation of permanent employment.
cases.dec_b: DEFER; reapply once probation is cleared.
